title: The same force speeds up a heavier object less
summary: NASA Glenn says that, for equal forces, a heavier object accelerates less than a lighter one.
body: NASA Glenn writes the constant-mass form of the second law as force equals mass times acceleration. The guide says this holds when mass stays constant, as with a baseball, and not when mass changes, as with a bottle rocket burning fuel. Under that constant-mass form, acceleration is proportional to the force and inversely proportional to the mass. For equal forces, a heavier object experiences less acceleration than a lighter object. Page last updated 27 June 2024.

sources.title: Newton's Laws of Motion
sources.author: Nancy Hall, NASA Glenn Research Center
sources.note: Public-domain NASA Glenn page, last updated 27 June 2024. Paraphrase of F = ma for constant mass and the heavier-versus-lighter comparison.
